findings.title: gate_review_capped sentence edited in two files isn't added to crossHostInvariants
findings.detail: Task 4 edits the identical `gate_review_capped is a spec or plan review after three review rounds...` sentence in commands/takt.md:39 and hosts/copilot/skills/takt/SKILL.md:40, and the task note correctly observes crossHostInvariants (internal/prompt/prompt_test.go:84) doesn't cover it so no test edit is 'needed'. But that list exists precisely to catch one file drifting from the other on a hand-maintained sentence like this one (see the list's own doc comment at line 78-83). As written, if a future edit changes this sentence in only one of the two files, TestPromptNamesEveryOpGateStepAndReason and TestPromptInvariantsReadTheSameOnEveryHost would both still pass — the former only checks that the gate id token `gate_review_capped` appears, not the surrounding prose. This is a real, currently-unpinned gap that intersects the exact line this diff changed.

findings.title: Option-count assertion doesn't verify option identity
findings.detail: TestPlanReviewRoundsAreCapped checks `len(choices) != 3` but never checks the actual Choice values/order (e.g. accept/retry/stop), so a bug in questionGateReviewCapped that returned three wrong options (or the wrong order) would still pass this test. This exactly mirrors the same weak assertion in the precedent TestSpecReviewRoundsAreCapped (internal/decide/decide_test.go:1099), so it's a pre-existing pattern rather than a new regression, but since decide_plan_cap_test.go is new code in this diff and free of the G7 no-edit constraint that applies to decide_test.go, it could have asserted `slices.Equal(choices, []string{"accept", "retry", "stop"})` (as another test does at decide_test.go:987 for a related gate) for a stronger guarantee.
